data.gender_notes: Balajee is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Balajee is a name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'Lord of Strength'. In Hindu mythology, Balajee is an epithet of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe. He is also known as 'Balarama', the elder brother of Lord Krishna, who embodies strength and courage. The name Balajee carries the meaning “Lord of Strength” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Balajee usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balajee total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Balajee is a name that evokes the strength and power of Lord Balaji, a form of Lord Venkateswara. It symbolizes the protection and guidance of the divine in one's life, bringing prosperity, wisdom, and courage.

historical_references.reference: Balaji is a name of Lord Venkateswara or Lord Balaji, a form of Lord Vishnu. The name Balaji means 'Lord of the Little Village' or 'Lord of the Child'. The name is believed to have originated from the legend that Lord Venkateswara appeared as a little boy to the sage Bhogar in the hills of Tirumala, near Tirupati, in the 9th or 10th century CE.
historical_references.context: Legend of Lord Venkateswara's appearance as a child

historical_references.reference: Balaji is also known as the presiding deity of the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple, which is one of the most famous pilgrimage sites for Hindus. The temple is believed to have been in existence since the 11th or 12th century CE and has been an important center of Hindu pilgrimage for over 1,000 years.
